case: Deterministic state preservation across script reload
requirement: Covered and baseline output/state agree, including state on an instance created before instrumentation reloads its script
notes: Isolates gd-tools 0.4.0's own stated mechanism -- Script.reload(true) on an already-running autoload's script, called from coverage.gd's addon _ready() -- from its source-rewriting step, which this fixture does not perform (the script's source is unchanged across the reload call). Result on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 build: reload(true) preserves both object identity (same_instance=true) and mutated instance-variable state (counter carries 11 into the reload and reaches 111 afterward, matching the no-reload baseline exactly) with reload_err=0. This is a real, engine-version-specific finding, not an assumption: it means the reload mechanism itself is sound on this engine build, so if BP04 finds gd-tools mishandling state, the defect is in the source-rewriting/injection step or in something reload(true) does NOT preserve (e.g. running scripts with active coroutines, or non-Node RefCounted instances, which this fixture does not exercise), not in reload(true) itself.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
ambiguities: Only tested on a Node-based autoload with plain instance variables. A RefCounted instance holding a live coroutine (interacts with F045/F046) or a Resource with exported properties are separate, unbuilt variants.

Does not test reload(true) when the on-disk source has actually changed (gd-tools' real use case, since it rewrites the file before reloading). This fixture only shows the reload mechanism preserves state when the source is unchanged; a changed-source variant belongs with the real adapter in BP04.
